agent-goal-verifier.advantage: Narrower and more frequent than whole-PR review, making it useful for exploring inexpensive continuous checks.
agent-goal-verifier.limitation: The author explicitly calls this early experimentation with benchmarking still to come. A completion judgment is not a passed test; false-stop and missed-error rates are unknown.
agent-goal-verifier.reported_result: The author says Jev replaces a more expensive reasoning model and permits more frequent checks, without a complete quality/cost comparison.
agent-goal-verifier.media_note: The main post has a roughly 17-second video. A promised guide is not treated as already delivered.
agent-goal-verifier.review_summary: Supports an early verifier prototype, not universal verification suitability or proven long-horizon gains.

drape-outfit-selection.title: Drape try-on experiment: select outfits from speech
drape-outfit-selection.summary: Choose clothes from speech and wardrobe information, then display the change through a video system.
drape-outfit-selection.plain_explanation: Like a stylist choosing from a wardrobe list: Jev selects clothes and a separate video stage puts them on screen.
drape-outfit-selection.mechanism: Author replies describe transcripts and existing clothing metadata as inputs, with reference garment images used by a realtime video-to-video stage. The experiment was not actually integrated into Drape.
drape-outfit-selection.advantage: Adds conversational selection and current-outfit context to ordinary product recommendation, with visual feedback.
drape-outfit-selection.limitation: The full video model, transcription pipeline and end-to-end bill are undisclosed. Selection latency and cost are not full try-on measurements.
drape-outfit-selection.reported_result: The author reports about 620ms and $0.0011 per Jev decision, excluding creation of pre-existing metadata.
drape-outfit-selection.media_note: The 31-second clip is combined with author replies about metadata, rendering and the lack of app integration.
drape-outfit-selection.review_summary: The author separates outfit decisions from video rendering; decision timing alone does not establish end-to-end realtime performance.

goodreads-taste-prediction.title: Goodreads: predict personal five-star books
goodreads-taste-prediction.summary: Use past ratings to predict which books one reader might award five stars.
goodreads-taste-prediction.plain_explanation: Like showing a bookseller your reading diary and asking for a guess; this tests one person’s taste.
goodreads-taste-prediction.mechanism: The author starts with roughly 1,000 personal Goodreads ratings, holds out 100, and compares Jev with GPT-5.6 on five-star prediction. Prompts, split details and class balance are not established.
goodreads-taste-prediction.advantage: Uses personal preference labels and describes a holdout, unlike generic categorization; useful for exploring personalized decisions.
goodreads-taste-prediction.limitation: A 100-item single-reader test does not establish general recommendation quality. Majority-class baselines, leakage, precision and recall still need checking.
goodreads-taste-prediction.reported_result: The author reports slightly better accuracy, 53-fold lower cost and 25-fold greater speed for this setup; not independently reproduced.
goodreads-taste-prediction.media_note: The post includes a roughly 12-second results demo; separate from the same author’s property-filtering task.
goodreads-taste-prediction.review_summary: Data and holdout sizes are stated, but the full protocol is missing; the ratios do not generalize to other readers or tasks.

zillow-semantic-filters.title: Zillow listings: natural-language filters
zillow-semantic-filters.summary: Organize listings by architecture, renovation status and other nonstandard filters.
zillow-semantic-filters.plain_explanation: Like attaching labels to a stack of listings: translate a spoken requirement into questions, then keep matching properties.
zillow-semantic-filters.mechanism: The author describes semantic classification by style, renovation and freeway proximity. Raw fields, geographic inputs and any image-to-text preparation are undisclosed.
zillow-semantic-filters.advantage: More flexible than fixed checkboxes and better suited to bulk judgments than individual chats.
zillow-semantic-filters.limitation: No labeled test set or error breakdown. This does not establish direct photo input to Jev or verified map-distance measurement.
zillow-semantic-filters.reported_result: The author reports thousands of listings in under 20 seconds for $0.18; inclusion of retrieval and preprocessing is unknown.
zillow-semantic-filters.media_note: A roughly 23-second original demo, independent of the same author’s Goodreads prediction experiment.
zillow-semantic-filters.review_summary: Supports custom property tagging, with accuracy, input provenance and full billing boundaries still unresolved.

shiori-link-tagging.title: Shiori: automatic bookmark tags
shiori-link-tagging.summary: Categorize saved links so they are easier to find by topic later.
shiori-link-tagging.plain_explanation: Like organizing a bookmark drawer: read the available page information and choose topic compartments.
shiori-link-tagging.mechanism: The author shows Jev versus Haiku for Shiori link tagging. Page extraction, label vocabulary and multilabel rules were not established.
shiori-link-tagging.advantage: Applies classification directly to bookmark retrieval; speed, incorrect tags and missing tags can be evaluated separately.
shiori-link-tagging.limitation: The video lacks labeled data and matched-condition statistics. Faster interface updates do not establish equal tag quality.
shiori-link-tagging.reported_result: A roughly 25-second comparison clip, without reproducible accuracy, cost or speedup figures.
shiori-link-tagging.media_note: Only the tagging feature is collected; other Shiori features are not assumed to use Jev.
shiori-link-tagging.review_summary: The task and comparison media are clear, but superiority over Haiku or production-quality classification is unproven.

jev-align.title: jev-align: refine decision criteria with human feedback
jev-align.summary: Label boundary cases and iteratively improve Jev’s decision instructions.
jev-align.plain_explanation: Like revising a marking guide with an assistant: you supply answers, another model proposes wording, Jev evaluates it, and you accept or reject the change.
jev-align.mechanism: The pinned CLI samples uncertain examples and random audit rows. GEPA optimizes task specifications against human labels using a separate reflection model; it does not fine-tune Jev weights.
jev-align.advantage: Adds feedback, diff inspection and rollback to manual prompting, supporting binary, multiclass, multilabel and ordered-score tasks.
jev-align.limitation: Training gains do not guarantee generalization. Held-out evaluation is optional; annotation, reflection and repeated evaluation costs must also be counted.
jev-align.reported_result: Source and a roughly two-minute demo support the workflow; this catalog has not reproduced it or established a universal gain.
jev-align.media_note: Launch posts and quotes refer to one tool. Pinned sources preserve the inspected version.
jev-align.review_summary: Code exposes labeling, GEPA’s optimization target and human acceptance. A denotes clear implementation evidence, not proven generalization gains.

third-hand.title: Third Hand / arc-cua: choose actions on a Mac
third-hand.summary: Read controls and screen text, choose actions and enter request- or planner-supplied text.
third-hand.plain_explanation: A planner supplies the task and a note, Jev chooses from a control list, and the executor handles clicks, typing and waiting.
third-hand.mechanism: Third Hand is a Swift app; the same author’s arc-cua is a separate Python executor reusing its text-entry approach. An upstream planner supplies goals, literal values and checks; AX/local OCR observes, Jev selects actions and input keys, and the runtime waits for UI stability.
third-hand.advantage: Third Hand extracts text from requests without another generator; arc-cua accepts literals from an upstream planner for agent integration. Both separate action selection from local execution.
third-hand.limitation: Separate repositories and programs are grouped as related work by one author. arc-cua still observes and calls Jev at each step; it has not established solved computer use. Unlabeled graphical interfaces and full-task success rates remain gaps.
third-hand.reported_result: The author shows a 31-second demo and claims subsecond latency. Documentation calls it experimental and says completion still needs human judgment.
third-hand.media_note: Preserves the Third Hand original snapshot, adding arc-cua’s 11-second demo, release reply and separate repository.
third-hand.review_summary: A concerns inspectable implementation roles. arc-cua explicitly reuses Third Hand’s text-entry approach and is grouped as related work. Solved computer use and universal speed gains lack benchmarks.

mujoco-apple-control.title: MuJoCo: three-model apple pick-and-place comparison
mujoco-apple-control.summary: Move an apple onto a plate with a simulated arm and compare direction and gripper decisions.
mujoco-apple-control.plain_explanation: The model directs movement and grasping; code solves joints and advances physics.
mujoco-apple-control.mechanism: Each pinned-version cycle makes two requests: intent, then XYZ signs and open/hold/close. Inputs are simulator geometry and contact feedback. Shared code handles step size, IK and physics, not camera perception or generated joint torques.
mujoco-apple-control.advantage: Unlike a short dual-arm demo, this publishes responses, trajectories, source snapshots, success criteria and an offline verification entry point.
mujoco-apple-control.limitation: Only one seed-0 trial per controller, so success rates are unknown. Replay synchronizes simulation time and removes API waits; video duration is not task wall time.
mujoco-apple-control.reported_result: Recorded results: Jev completed in 181.847s for $0.018825; GPT-6 Astra in 707.274s for $5.933624; GPT-4.1 mini reached 160 cycles. The roughly 1/315 cost applies only to these records.
mujoco-apple-control.media_note: The minute-long comparison and protocol replies form one case. Mini came from an earlier paired run with the same initial scene, not one simultaneous three-model run.
mujoco-apple-control.review_summary: Pinned sources disclose single-trial limits, controller responsibilities and replay timing. A indicates inspectability; this catalog ran neither verification nor physical robots.

voice-spell-game.title: Voice-spell game: turn a spoken chant into magic
voice-spell-game.summary: Let semantic judgments determine the type and power of a player’s invented spell.
voice-spell-game.plain_explanation: Like a game referee interpreting a shouted move and letting game rules display the effect.
voice-spell-game.mechanism: The author assigns spell validity, element, form and power to Jev, then maps results to game parameters. Speech transcription and rendering are surrounding stages whose implementations were not established.
voice-spell-game.advantage: Explores open language input mapped to finite game parameters, instead of fixed buttons or model-controlled play.
voice-spell-game.limitation: Scoring rules, false activations and consistency need testing. No evidence that Jev directly processes audio or generates visual effects.
voice-spell-game.reported_result: A roughly 75-second proof-of-concept clip without reproducible end-to-end latency or cost measurements.
voice-spell-game.media_note: A distinct interaction goal from character chat and gameplay agents, grouped as a separate game prototype.
voice-spell-game.review_summary: The post specifies judgment dimensions and parameter mapping; playability, recognition quality and stability remain unverified.

emotion-topic-chat-game.title: Chat game: classify emotion and topic
emotion-topic-chat-game.summary: Classify a player’s emotion and topic to drive a chat game’s response.
emotion-topic-chat-game.plain_explanation: Like signposts in a conversation game: identify the subject and tone, then let the game choose a response.
emotion-topic-chat-game.mechanism: The author explicitly assigns emotion/topic classification to Jev and provides a Cloudflare-hosted entry point. Response-text sources, branching rules and candidate counts are unestablished.
emotion-topic-chat-game.advantage: Uses coarser dialogue-state decisions than character-by-character chat generation.
emotion-topic-chat-game.limitation: A free public page does not imply permanently free underlying service. Full costs, classification errors and long-dialogue consistency are unknown; replies are not assumed to be generated by Jev.
emotion-topic-chat-game.reported_result: The author describes low costs and provides a 21-second clip and public demo. This catalog did not run it or call the model.
emotion-topic-chat-game.media_note: One game, with emotion and topic judgments kept together.
emotion-topic-chat-game.review_summary: Supports an emotion/topic-driven prototype; sustainable free operation and long-term dialogue quality are not established.

canada-word-map.title: Canada word map: visualize regional associations
canada-word-map.summary: Enter a word and display Canadian regions the model associates with it.
canada-word-map.plain_explanation: Like putting association notes on a map, not surveying local residents.
canada-word-map.mechanism: The author describes Jev predicting word-associated regions for a map display. Geographic candidates, prompts and score normalization are undisclosed.
canada-word-map.advantage: Like word-to-color judgments, it visualizes semantics, but uses geographic regions as outputs.
canada-word-map.limitation: Subjective associations are not demographic, cultural or regional facts. No reference set or calibration is provided.
canada-word-map.reported_result: The author reports instant responses and under one cent, without call counts or timing boundaries.
canada-word-map.media_note: A separate 23-second map demo. It quotes the color experiment but has a different author, task and media.
canada-word-map.review_summary: Shows model associations; understanding Canada is not an established geography or social-knowledge capability.

contextual-clipboard.title: Contextual clipboard: choose what to paste now
contextual-clipboard.summary: Use the active field and app context to select an item from clipboard history.
contextual-clipboard.plain_explanation: Like finding the right note in a stack: inspect the field you are filling and match an existing snippet.
contextual-clipboard.mechanism: The author supplies clipboard history plus field/app context to Jev. Capture interfaces, candidate lengths and execution confirmation are unknown.
contextual-clipboard.advantage: Like shell-history suggestions, it reuses existing text, but targets fields across applications.
contextual-clipboard.limitation: Only a prototype and subjective accuracy impression; similar candidates, errors and sensitive-content filtering need testing. It is not established as offline.
contextual-clipboard.reported_result: The author calls it a travel-time toy that seems accurate, without measured hit rate or cost.
contextual-clipboard.media_note: Original demonstration media is attached; candidate selection is not unrestricted text generation.
contextual-clipboard.review_summary: Task, input sources and media are clear; accuracy, privacy handling and cross-app reliability remain unresolved.

x-draft-hype-check.title: X draft check: flag overhyped wording before posting
x-draft-hype-check.summary: Warn when a draft sounds like exaggerated marketing or a sales pitch.
x-draft-hype-check.plain_explanation: Like an editor checking whether a draft overdoes its tone; this judges style, not factual truth.
x-draft-hype-check.mechanism: The author built a browser extension using Jev to assess the style of an X draft. Labels, prompts and trigger frequency are undisclosed.
x-draft-hype-check.advantage: Supports revision before publication, rather than trying to predict reach.
x-draft-hype-check.limitation: Style is subjective and does not establish profession, motives or factual accuracy. Human agreement and false-positive rates are missing.
x-draft-hype-check.reported_result: A roughly 44-second extension demo, without reproducible accuracy or cost figures.
x-draft-hype-check.media_note: An original implementation and video, distinct from feed filtering and virality prediction.
x-draft-hype-check.review_summary: Supports a draft-style reminder, not fact-checking or reliable judgments about people.

ori-task-classification.title: Ori Eval: compare 30-way request classification
ori-task-classification.summary: Classify requests into 30 task types and compare five models on speed, cost and correctness.
ori-task-classification.plain_explanation: Like sorting the same letters into 30 inboxes and comparing mistakes and time.
ori-task-classification.mechanism: OpenRouter describes sequential, stateless evaluation on the same 200 synthetic cases. LLM reasoning was off except for GLM 5.3 Flash, which ran at low effort.
ori-task-classification.advantage: Discloses the task, sample size, synthetic origin and some settings, and acknowledges that Jev is not the cheapest model.
ori-task-classification.limitation: Complete examples, per-case labels and repeated runs are absent. Default provider routing affects some tail latencies, limiting production generalization.
ori-task-classification.reported_result: The author reports over five times the speed of the runner-up, accuracy within a few cases across models, and second-lowest cost behind Qwen3.8 Flash.
ori-task-classification.media_note: The main chart and four methodological/results replies form one request-classification experiment, not a general agent-quality judge.
ori-task-classification.review_summary: The task and important limits are stated, but a small synthetic set and incomplete reproduction materials restrict the conclusions.

docjev.title: DocJev: classify documents and split bundles
docjev.summary: Identify document types and boundaries inside a combined PDF.
docjev.plain_explanation: OCR reads the pages; Jev decides their categories and where another document starts.
docjev.mechanism: Pinned code uses Choice for categories and Noul for page boundaries. LiteParse can parse locally; Jev decisions remain hosted, with LlamaParse optional.
docjev.advantage: Adds page-boundary detection to ordinary document classification, with an inspectable small evaluation.
docjev.limitation: Only 40 short English PDFs and eight constructed packets; labels lack human review. This does not establish scan, long-document or production accuracy.
docjev.reported_result: Published results: both classify 40/40; packet exact match is 7/8 for Jev and 8/8 for Luna. Decision medians are 138.6/794.3ms and 209.6/1352.3ms, excluding OCR.
docjev.media_note: A 24-second post video plus pinned code and evaluation.
docjev.review_summary: Implementation and timing scope are clear. Equal accuracy and roughly sixfold speed claims need qualification: splitting differs and OCR is excluded.

dasheng-reading.title: ReadAloud: check missing words and changed meaning
dasheng-reading.summary: Transcribe reading and mark omissions or questionable substitutions for practice.
dasheng-reading.plain_explanation: Compare a transcript with the passage; text can reveal meaning changes but cannot establish pronunciation quality.
dasheng-reading.mechanism: R2T2 transcribes speech; code aligns words. Jev judges suspicious-word equivalence, error type and meaning; local formulas score completeness, pace and the total.
dasheng-reading.advantage: Word-level feedback makes omissions easier to inspect than a plain transcript.
dasheng-reading.limitation: Pinned code calls hosted Jev through ZenMux. The full stack is not offline and does not score pronunciation, stress or accent; validation against professional speaking assessment is absent.
dasheng-reading.reported_result: An approximately 81-second demo accompanies a claim to replace an English-speaking app; the code supports a narrower reading-text checker.
dasheng-reading.media_note: Original post and pinned scoring code form one case; neither ASR nor model calls were run.
dasheng-reading.review_summary: Inspectable implementation, but full-product replacement and fully offline wording exceed the implemented assessment and network behavior.

needle-semantic-find.title: Needle: find webpage passages by meaning
needle-semantic-find.summary: Use your own words to find relevant sentences without remembering exact keywords.
needle-semantic-find.plain_explanation: Like asking someone to highlight useful passages: read the page text and select the best source sentence.
needle-semantic-find.mechanism: The extension extracts passages. A backend calls Jev through Vercel AI Gateway for relevance and sentence selection, then maps highlights back; the inclusion threshold is 0.58.
needle-semantic-find.advantage: Handles paraphrases while keeping results tied to inspectable source text.
needle-semantic-find.limitation: Limited to 160 passages and 60,000 characters; PDF viewers and scans are unsupported. Long pages may be incomplete. Queries and captured passages go to hosted services; the threshold does not guarantee recall.
needle-semantic-find.reported_result: A roughly 21-second demo, without a standard retrieval benchmark. Temporary promotions are not permanent free access.
needle-semantic-find.media_note: The author links the Needle subdirectory; the entire awesome-llm-apps repository is not counted as another application.
needle-semantic-find.review_summary: Pinned code establishes extraction, relevance and sentence selection. A reflects clear implementation, not verified search completeness.

reddit-radar-mcp.title: Reddit Radar MCP: filter discussions by your criteria
reddit-radar-mcp.summary: Find Reddit discussions matching custom criteria from Claude Code or Codex.
reddit-radar-mcp.plain_explanation: A sorter collects posts, applies your criteria and returns matching discussions.
reddit-radar-mcp.mechanism: The author describes an MCP tool combining Reddit scanning with Jev classification. Coverage, deduplication, label definitions and source remain unestablished.
reddit-radar-mcp.advantage: Brings bulk filtering into existing assistants for exploring discussion topics.
reddit-radar-mcp.limitation: Public discussion alone does not validate demand. Precision, recall and full collection/inference costs are missing.
reddit-radar-mcp.reported_result: The author claims tens of thousands of posts in minutes and shows a roughly 12-second clip; throughput and idea validation are unverified.
reddit-radar-mcp.media_note: One original MCP product demo, not separate apps for each client.
reddit-radar-mcp.review_summary: A clear task and demo, with scale and business outcomes remaining author claims.

toothless-voice-gate.title: Toothless: decide whether speech addresses the assistant
toothless-voice-gate.summary: Separate assistant-directed remarks from people talking to each other.
toothless-voice-gate.plain_explanation: Like a considerate listener, use conversational context to decide whether to respond.
toothless-voice-gate.mechanism: The author describes simultaneous checks for topic continuation, internet needs and potential assistant usefulness. Transcription, speaker information and the final activation rule are not fully disclosed.
toothless-voice-gate.advantage: Shares wake-word-free interaction with CNVS, emphasizing when to join a multi-person conversation.
toothless-voice-gate.limitation: No multi-speaker false-activation or miss rates. This does not establish direct audio understanding by Jev or reliable addressee recognition.
toothless-voice-gate.reported_result: A roughly 3m40s prototype demo, without controlled latency, quality or all-day evaluation.
toothless-voice-gate.media_note: Independent author and media, grouped with CNVS rather than treated as its update.
toothless-voice-gate.review_summary: Supports an activation-gate prototype; natural turn-taking and persistent reliability remain unverified.

mario-lightgbm-teacher.title: Mario teacher data: Jev demonstrates, LightGBM takes over
mario-lightgbm-teacher.summary: Generate examples with a teacher model, then let local LightGBM play Mario; the author later changed teachers.
mario-lightgbm-teacher.plain_explanation: A coach demonstrates and a trainee takes over; the trainee runs during gameplay.
mario-lightgbm-teacher.mechanism: The original uses Jev teacher data to train LightGBM. A follow-up reports better results with DeepSeek-4.1-Flash outputs in the same harness. LightGBM still runs gameplay; data and training code are undisclosed.
mario-lightgbm-teacher.advantage: Moves network waiting to preparation instead of every gameplay decision, unlike continuously calling Jev.
mario-lightgbm-teacher.limitation: No matched dataset sizes, unseen-level evaluation or repeated-run records across teachers. These are not intrinsic Jev speedups; preparation and training costs are unknown.
mario-lightgbm-teacher.reported_result: The earlier Jev-teacher version claimed over 300-fold speedup. The update reports repeated original failures, then over 1,000-fold speed and consistent completion with DeepSeek teaching. The latter is not a new Jev achievement; neither claim is independently verified.
mario-lightgbm-teacher.media_note: Keep the original 22-second clip and add the 23-second teacher-switch demo, not another Jev application.
mario-lightgbm-teacher.review_summary: Merge contrary follow-up evidence from the same author and harness. Preserve the original while identifying the switch to DeepSeek; its new completion claim cannot be credited to Jev.

minecraft-fixed-route.title: Minecraft fixed route: planning plus bounded actions
minecraft-fixed-route.summary: Combine a planner, Jev and pathfinding code on a known route to the dragon.
minecraft-fixed-route.plain_explanation: Follow a surveyed map: the planner sets objectives, Jev picks an operation and pathfinding handles movement.
minecraft-fixed-route.mechanism: Astra plans, Jev selects bounded actions and Mineflayer executes. A fixed seed and Peaceful difficulty use configured supply/active-portal coordinates plus a read-only dragon-position sensor.
minecraft-fixed-route.advantage: Inspectable route and control roles; a separate implementation from the existing Minecraft hybrid controller.
minecraft-fixed-route.limitation: Neither random-world exploration nor individual-key/screenshot control. Full video and action logs remain local to the author; the short public clip cannot establish the complete run or bill.
minecraft-fixed-route.reported_result: The author reports 8m43s and $0.01 Jev plus $0.96 Astra. Documentation adds surveyed routes and scripts; this catalog has not reproduced it.
minecraft-fixed-route.media_note: The 39-second post and author reply form one case; full run evidence is absent from the repository.
minecraft-fixed-route.review_summary: The WASD/mouse claim conflicts with documented structured-state, higher-level actions. Treat this as a bounded route experiment, not general autonomous completion.

token-choice-loop.title: Token-choice loop: assemble text through repeated decisions
token-choice-loop.summary: Repeatedly ask Jev to choose the next token from candidates.
token-choice-loop.plain_explanation: Build a sentence by choosing one piece from a tray at each step.
token-choice-loop.mechanism: The author places Jev in an autoregressive loop with possible next tokens. The full vocabulary, stopping rule and sampling procedure are undisclosed.
token-choice-loop.advantage: Complements word- and character-choice experiments, illustrating how candidate granularity affects assembled text.
token-choice-loop.limitation: No language-quality, total-call or full-response latency comparison. This is not a native generation endpoint or established chat model.
token-choice-loop.reported_result: A roughly 22-second demo; the author cautiously says it partly works, without general performance conclusions.
token-choice-loop.media_note: Independent author and media, grouped with word/character loops; reposts are not separate cases.
token-choice-loop.review_summary: A sourced loop and prototype, with text quality and efficiency still unverified.

jev-field-notes-curation.title: Jev Field Notes: curate Jev examples with Jev
jev-field-notes-curation.summary: Select X application demos for a community collection.
jev-field-notes-curation.plain_explanation: Like a clipping editor, collect leads and decide which ones to keep.
jev-field-notes-curation.mechanism: The author describes automatic X discovery and Jev curation. A public resource page exists; retrieval, ranking, deduplication and quality criteria are not established.
jev-field-notes-curation.advantage: Applies classification to a concrete editorial task, comparable with bookmark tagging and bulk post screening.
jev-field-notes-curation.limitation: Update automation and curation quality are unverified. Popularity does not establish truth; original sources and implementation still need checking.
jev-field-notes-curation.reported_result: An approximately eight-second preview; the public resource page was checked, but its scheduled backend was not.
jev-field-notes-curation.media_note: One curation tool; its collected demos are not counted again as new projects.
jev-field-notes-curation.review_summary: Supports an author-described curation prototype, not established completeness, deduplication or fact-checking capability.

animeact-jev-demo.title: AnimeAct: connect dialogue to character acting
animeact-jev-demo.summary: Connect dialogue intent to a 3D acting system for responsive expressions and motion.
animeact-jev-demo.plain_explanation: Like a director cueing an actor: interpret a line, then let the acting engine execute expressions and movement.
animeact-jev-demo.mechanism: The author demos Jev with AnimeAct Engine. The product page describes expression, gaze and upper-body composition plus JSON control; the fields Jev selects are undisclosed.
animeact-jev-demo.advantage: Adds visible character feedback to classification, useful for exploring dialogue-driven acting.
animeact-jev-demo.limitation: Do not attribute all animation or audio processing to Jev. Stage timings, quality benchmarks and a runnable Jev integration are missing.
animeact-jev-demo.reported_result: The author describes near-realtime behavior and tester recruitment, not an independently verified production integration.
animeact-jev-demo.media_note: A September 19 original discovered through a newer quote, with video and images; quotations are not extra cases.
animeact-jev-demo.review_summary: A sourced integration demo, with exact interface and release availability unresolved. Future-dated product-page text is not evidence of a completed launch.

astra-ares.title: Astra-Ares: adjust reasoning effort as work progresses
astra-ares.summary: Give Codex more reasoning effort for difficult steps and less for routine ones.
astra-ares.plain_explanation: Like changing gears for the same problem solver: Jev reads the task and recent tool feedback to select the next effort level.
astra-ares.mechanism: A patched Codex CLI asks Jev through a local bridge before the next model generation. It selects effort and a 1/2/5/10-step lease, rechecking after new input or tool failures while keeping model identity fixed.
astra-ares.advantage: Finer control than choosing a model once per task, with inspectable switching conditions and context boundaries.
astra-ares.limitation: An early preview requiring a patched CLI, not intervention inside one generation. Validation explicitly excludes workload savings and cache hit rates; halving cost is not guaranteed.
astra-ares.reported_result: The post reports 50% lower Astra cost. Repository validation covers native settings application and prefix preservation, not a controlled savings benchmark.
astra-ares.media_note: The 23-second original and source-release reply are one case; pinned code was read, not installed.
astra-ares.review_summary: A covers the inspectable controller. Savings and faster runs remain author measurements; preserving prompt structure does not establish cache hit rates.

webctl.title: webctl: filter web results before the research assistant reads them
webctl.summary: Remove irrelevant and near-duplicate search material before it reaches an assistant.
webctl.plain_explanation: Sort a stack of clippings first: pick relevant pages, merge repeats and pass useful passages to the answer-writing model.
webctl.mechanism: Search providers retrieve results; code collapses identical URLs/titles, and Jev scores relevance and confirms near-duplicates. Optional scraping adds chunk filtering; a separate model can summarize.
webctl.advantage: Targets multi-page research, complementing Needle’s source-sentence highlighting on one page; code and a small evaluation are inspectable.
webctl.limitation: Only 30 questions and one run per cell, with a model judge rather than human ground truth. Jev and summarizer calls are separately billed and excluded from token counts; context reduction is not full-stack savings.
webctl.reported_result: The report shows lower costs and higher judge scores for three Claude Code configurations. The same Kimi model judges pi answers, introducing bias.
webctl.media_note: Original image plus pinned code and evaluation; no search or model APIs were run.
webctl.review_summary: A reflects inspectable filtering and evaluation boundaries. Small samples, single runs and separate billing do not establish universal accuracy or cost gains.

jimothy.title: Jimothy: teach a local classifier from Jev examples
jimothy.summary: Collect Jev decisions for a specific task and train a small classifier for local browser or server use.
jimothy.plain_explanation: A teacher marks examples, then a specialist apprentice learns that particular kind of question.
jimothy.mechanism: Read saved labels or call Jev through Gateway with response caching. Train a head on MiniLM features or TF-IDF, separating model selection, calibration and acceptance-threshold evaluation.
jimothy.advantage: Useful for repetitive, stable classification tasks; provides training and export tooling beyond a one-off teacher-data experiment.
jimothy.limitation: The local student is not Jev weights. Applications must implement Jev fallback. Thresholds measure agreement with supplied labels, not guaranteed correctness or robustness to changed data.
jimothy.reported_result: The post claims 15–45MB and 10–20-fold speedups. Repository timing examples use warmed single-input inference on an M3 Max, excluding loading, teacher collection and training.
jimothy.media_note: A 21-second demo with pinned teacher interface and training documentation; no training or exported inference was run.
jimothy.review_summary: A covers inspectable data and training roles. Student inference speed is not full-pipeline speed, and teacher errors may be inherited.

perch.title: Perch: check code against natural-language rules
perch.summary: Check behavioral expectations and rank suspicious defects for human or agent review.
perch.plain_explanation: Read code with a checklist: map functions and calls, then ask whether each expectation is satisfied.
perch.mechanism: tree-sitter builds a method/call graph. Jev uses Noul, Choice and Score for defect likelihood, location and severity; natural-language ensure rules join checks and changes can be rechecked.
perch.advantage: Addresses behavioral requirements that ordinary syntax rules struggle to express, beyond comment scoring.
perch.limitation: Probability rankings are not defect proofs; independent detection benchmarks are absent. Neighbor context is bounded and long methods have an eight-pass cap; inspect partial-read and failure records.
perch.reported_result: A roughly 13-second behavior-driven development demo, with public scan code and documented scoring and coverage.
perch.media_note: Independent author/repository, compared with existing ESLint experiments; no project was scanned.
perch.review_summary: A covers inspectable scanning and rules. Confidence does not establish a real bug; diagnosis, reproduction and regression checks remain necessary.

presentation-coach.title: Presentation coach: track points still left to cover
presentation-coach.summary: Follow a presentation against slides and notes, flagging material not yet covered.
presentation-coach.plain_explanation: Like a partner holding your outline, follow what you have said and mark the remaining points.
presentation-coach.mechanism: The author describes comparing speech with slides and notes using Jev to track coverage; the transcription component and input schema are undisclosed.
presentation-coach.advantage: Focuses on live reminders rather than after-meeting summaries, useful for presentation practice.
presentation-coach.limitation: The author explicitly says it exists only in a local copy of Slides and is not live. This does not establish direct Jev audio processing or reliable delivery assessment.
presentation-coach.reported_result: A roughly 3-minute-5-second demo, without omission rates, transcription-error analysis or end-to-end timing.
presentation-coach.media_note: Original demo and the author’s not-yet-live reply are merged; this is not a released product.
presentation-coach.review_summary: A clear prototype and task; public availability and real-presentation accuracy remain unverified.

kaku-note-tags.title: Kaku: tag notes using your existing organization
kaku-note-tags.summary: Organize notes with workspace tags and send uncertain matches for human review.
kaku-note-tags.plain_explanation: Like an archivist: apply obvious labels first and collect doubtful ones for you to check.
kaku-note-tags.mechanism: The author describes batch Jev judgments against existing tags, applying high-confidence matches and reviewing low-confidence cells in a matrix, with diff confirmation, discard and snapshot rollback.
kaku-note-tags.advantage: Keeps the user’s tag vocabulary. Unlike Shiori’s web bookmarks, Kaku targets note libraries.
kaku-note-tags.limitation: Confidence is not measured labeling accuracy. Human-reference comparisons, missed tags and cross-library validation are absent. Targeting Obsidian users does not establish an Obsidian plugin.
kaku-note-tags.reported_result: A roughly 31-second demo, with author replies describing batch judgments and review.
kaku-note-tags.media_note: Original, product link and workflow replies form one Kaku case; the app was not installed.
kaku-note-tags.review_summary: The task and review workflow have author support; large-scale quality, costs and exact model settings remain unverified.

semantic-edit-consistency.title: Linked editing: find other passages affected by a change
semantic-edit-consistency.summary: After an edit, find related inconsistencies and suggest revisions.
semantic-edit-consistency.plain_explanation: Like an editor rereading a manuscript with the new facts in hand, looking for passages still using the old version.
semantic-edit-consistency.mechanism: The author combines Jev and Gemini Flash Lite to identify related edits and suggest fixes. Exact component roles, chunking and dependency rules are undisclosed.
semantic-edit-consistency.advantage: Unlike the same author’s Needle search highlighting, this prototype targets consistency after changes.
semantic-edit-consistency.limitation: An open-source Chrome extension is a stated plan, not a verified release. Long-document misses, incorrect suggestions and full round-trip timing are unmeasured.
semantic-edit-consistency.reported_result: A roughly 19-second near-realtime demo does not establish that every affected passage is found.
semantic-edit-consistency.media_note: A distinct editing task and demo from Needle; the planned extension is not another case.
semantic-edit-consistency.review_summary: Supports a linked-editing prototype, with complete coverage, latency and availability still unestablished.

higgsfield-voice-ads.title: Higgsfield: control an ad-production workflow by voice
higgsfield-voice-ads.summary: Use voice to connect product selection, image generation and video-ad creation.
higgsfield-voice-ads.plain_explanation: Give spoken directions to a production workflow whose components handle selection, assets and generated visuals.
higgsfield-voice-ads.mechanism: The official post adds voice control to a Jev ad workflow combining DeepSeek and Higgsfield. Exact Jev routing fields, transcription and generation boundaries are not fully disclosed.
higgsfield-voice-ads.advantage: Combines multiple production steps behind one input method, useful for studying decisions alongside generation tools.
higgsfield-voice-ads.limitation: Do not attribute image or video generation entirely to Jev. Source, repeated-task success, production quality and full-stack cost comparisons are missing.
higgsfield-voice-ads.reported_result: A roughly 38-second workflow demo, without a generalizable speed or quality benchmark.
higgsfield-voice-ads.media_note: An update to the author’s workflow but its first intake here; the full ad workflow counts once.
higgsfield-voice-ads.review_summary: Supports an integrated voice-ad demo. Exact roles and reliability remain unknown, so B is retained.

openclaw-decisions.title: OpenClaw: a shared decision interface for plugins
openclaw-decisions.summary: Let plugins or application code request classification, scoring and choices for later workflow steps.
openclaw-decisions.plain_explanation: Add a standard socket to a toolbox: code asks which option to choose, and an adapter sends the question to Jev.
openclaw-decisions.mechanism: The official article exposes api.runtime.decisions.evaluate in the Plugin SDK, backed by a configured decision model. Application code can now call directly, alongside the earlier agent-facing decision tool.
openclaw-decisions.advantage: A common plugin interface makes decisions reusable without requiring a chat model to initiate every judgment.
openclaw-decisions.limitation: Available in development checkouts; provider packages await a supporting release. Voice gating, tool filtering, compaction and routing are largely explorations or proposals, not all shipped features.
openclaw-decisions.reported_result: An official roughly 6-minute-51-second video and design article, without controlled throughput, cost or quality results.
openclaw-decisions.media_note: One Jev interface integration; another supported model and proposed plugins are not separate applications.
openclaw-decisions.review_summary: Official support for interface progress, with production release and proposed-use outcomes unverified. This is opt-in, not automatic activation of every feature.

sf-unreal-city.title: San Francisco city demo: animate a virtual neighborhood
sf-unreal-city.summary: Show people, pets and vehicles moving in an Unreal city scene.
sf-unreal-city.plain_explanation: Like assigning behavior in a model city: the scene presents the world while a decision layer chooses what happens next.
sf-unreal-city.mechanism: The author says Opus 5.5 built the San Francisco Unreal scene and Jev drives people, pets, cars and traffic. States, action candidates, scripts and scheduling remain unestablished.
sf-unreal-city.advantage: Illustrates several entity types rather than one NPC, useful for discussing decisions within simulations.
sf-unreal-city.limitation: The claim that Jev powers everything lacks implementation evidence. Rendering, physics and city generation cannot all be attributed to Jev; geographic accuracy and scale are unverified.
sf-unreal-city.reported_result: A 53-second demo; a follow-up reports $25 in Jev usage after leaving it running overnight accidentally. This does not establish per-entity or full-stack cost.
sf-unreal-city.media_note: Original and usage-cost reply are merged; the scene was not run and footage is not architecture proof.
sf-unreal-city.review_summary: C concerns the sweeping everything attribution. The city demo is retained, while component roles and scaling outcomes remain unknown.

btc-polymarket-paper.title: BTC paper trading: estimate five-minute direction from an order book
btc-polymarket-paper.summary: Read market order-book data, estimate direction and simulate trades against prediction-market prices.
btc-polymarket-paper.plain_explanation: Estimate a reference price, then compare it with a quoted price; faster execution cannot make a wrong estimate correct.
btc-polymarket-paper.mechanism: The author uses Binance BTC futures order-book data for Jev estimates of Polymarket five-minute directional-market fair value, trading on differences from quoted prices in a simulation.
btc-polymarket-paper.advantage: Connects decisions to explicit input and trading rules while clearly identifying paper trading, separate from live capital.
btc-polymarket-paper.limitation: No probability calibration, out-of-sample results or comparison including fees, latency and slippage. A model score is not established fair value, and a short demo cannot show profitability.
btc-polymarket-paper.reported_result: A 1,000u paper account and roughly 28-second demo, not verified real returns or live-fund trading.
btc-polymarket-paper.media_note: Original author video and a read-only demo link; no orders or bot runs were performed.
btc-polymarket-paper.review_summary: B supports a concrete paper-trading experiment only; predictive accuracy and profitability are unverified.

browser.title: Browser and computer control
browser.comparison: For browser loops, compare Browser Use and Stagehand: the former describes a dynamic DOM action space with text-generation fallback; the latter separates accessibility-tree observation from execution. For native apps, see CoreML/OCR. Cua currently offers a constrained semantic-action preview. agent-desktop retains an LLM for longer context; voice control and QA address different interaction needs. Runlayer emphasizes parallel sessions but lacks coverage and defect-detection evidence; Sac’s Calendar comparison focuses on one desktop task. Neither action video substitutes for acceptance assertions. Tester Army targets web/mobile testing but its open-source release is unverified; ego lite focuses on product filtering with a hybrid stack. Browser Use now includes a same-project WebMCP comparison: task coverage and per-attempt success are distinct. Sac’s new Jev-cu source now exposes accessibility-text observation and executor roles, resolving the earlier missing-interface detail; the fastest-in-Codex claim remains unverified. Third Hand enters text extracted from the request, TipTour’s Jev mode only clicks, and Ultrafast can use a small LLM for text entry. Their input capabilities differ; no-extra-LLM claims or step latency alone cannot rank them. arc-cua and Third Hand are grouped as related work by one author: the former receives planner-supplied literals, the latter extracts candidate text from requests. Assess full-task completion; fewer large-model calls do not mean no UI observation.
browser.flow: Observe the page or desktop → construct executable candidates → Jev selects → execute → observe again.
browser.analysis: DOM, accessibility trees and OCR are different observation interfaces. Keeping pixels local does not mean all content stays local. Browser Use still delegates text generation to an LLM. These designs come from author descriptions; unspecified encoding details remain unknown.
browser.evaluation: Compare the same read-only tasks using completion rate, steps, full elapsed time, total cost and recovery. Include unlabeled buttons, dynamic pages, dialogs and window changes. Do not compare one model decision with an entire task.

routing.title: Model, skill and tool routing
routing.comparison: Eve and Ephraim demonstrate model selection; Firstmate and local delegation address agent orchestration. Skillbox searches a skill library, Coding Garden connects everyday tools, and the Eve tool agent substitutes one stage of an existing system. ai-cli is an integration interface. These approaches can be combined. Hono JevRouter selects HTTP handlers using descriptions and the first qualifying route in registration order. Unlike model or skill selection, a routing error changes the response directly; it must not replace authentication. Codex Model Router selects a model and reasoning configuration each turn with documented fallback, but a user observed over-routing on easy tasks. Compare final quality, cache behavior and total bills, not classification speed alone. The Claude Code Mod defaults to subagent-model and main-effort routing, leaving main-model switching off. Compare cache effects, fallback and final quality separately from the Codex per-turn router. Astra-Ares adjusts one model’s effort between generations; OpenClaw exposes a shared plugin interface. Compare full-task quality, cost and cache hits for the former, and separate development interfaces from proposed uses for the latter.
routing.flow: Task text and candidate capabilities → Jev choice or scores → application checks candidates and constraints → invoke the selected model, skill or tool.
routing.analysis: Routing reduces the overhead of choosing an executor; the executor still does the work. Firstmate reports a small 25-task agreement study. Skillbox lacks retrieval-recall data. Deterministic invocation does not guarantee correct choices.
routing.evaluation: Use identical requests and measure routing suitability, final task quality, fallbacks, quota handling and total cost. Include requests with no suitable candidate.

review.title: Code quality and safety checks
review.comparison: Compare the 14-check PR reviewer, jev-review and jev-rabbit for explicit risks and escalation, iterative scoring and natural-language team rules respectively. Codebase classification examines overall structure. Command safety, jailbreak screening and upload checks guard different actions and need separate false-negative evaluations. The ESLint experiment judges snippet compliance; OpenCode permissions decide whether a tool action is allowed, questioned or denied before execution. They check different things and are not substitutes. Comment scoring separates accuracy from usefulness for clearer interpretation than one overall score, but currently shows only two trivial examples. ESLint checks snippets against rules, while PR tools cover broader changes. Compare their task scope and evidence size separately. Script.it scores diffs before generating explanations, reducing workflow overhead but recalling only 75% of confirmed bugs in its author evaluation. Compare both reduced false positives and increased misses with exploratory review. Goal verification checks turn-level completion; jev-align refines criteria with human labels. Measure false stops/misses for the former and held-out generalization for the latter, rather than treating training scores as reliability. Perch ranks behavioral defects beyond comment scoring and fixed syntax rules, increasing the need to reproduce flagged issues; high probability is not defect proof.
review.flow: Code or proposed action plus explicit rules → several narrow judgments → combine in code → notify, block or escalate.
review.analysis: The PR reviewer publishes an uncertainty-escalation rule, making it easier to inspect than an overall score. jev-review feedback can guide iterations, but a high score is not a passing test suite. Cheap screening does not remove the need to assess error costs.
review.evaluation: Measure false positives and negatives by risk type against independently labeled data. Test insufficient evidence, adversarial instructions, conflicting rules and uncertain results. Retain human review and static-tool baselines.

data.title: Data classification and organization
data.comparison: Email classification and DuckDB handle batches of text; the paper example includes generative preprocessing; Jev + Kimi shows uncertainty escalation. Payee cleanup is extraction/normalization and support intent is multi-question judgment. Their metrics are not interchangeable. Predictive spreadsheets put classification intent in column headings and emphasize live feedback. Compare interface response separately from full-table processing costs when considering DuckDB-style batching. The four-model email demo exposes differences in waiting time, while the 500-email case emphasizes batch scale and reported cost. The former lacks standardized accuracy and configuration evidence; the latter lacks a cross-model comparison. Times from separate demonstrations do not establish a ranking. The food notebook turns text into calorie and nutrient values. Like predictive spreadsheets it prioritizes immediate feedback, but numerical estimates also require trustworthy data and error evaluation; classification speed is not numerical accuracy. New cases cover tax-page identification, Box incident triage, Downloads filing, OCR-based image organization, Gmail intent search and snack scoring. Tax classification documents rejection gates and separate test sets; most others offer author timings. Accuracy cannot be ranked across unrelated datasets. Fictional interview notes demonstrate multidimensional classification. Per-record cost does not establish real hiring validity or fairness. Shiori tags bookmarks, Zillow adds listing labels, Goodreads predicts personal five-star preferences, and Ori Eval compares 30-way synthetic request classification. Evaluate tagging errors, field grounding, preference prediction and task labels separately; speed is not recommendation quality. DocJev targets categories and page boundaries, Reddit Radar screens discussions, and Jev Field Notes selects demos. Compare split errors, post precision/recall and source quality separately. DuckDB’s new speedup compares extension versions, not models. Kaku tags notes and Shiori tags web bookmarks; evaluate each label set. Jimothy trains local students from teacher labels, trading repeated inference efficiency against training and distribution shift. MotherDuck excludes NULLs from accuracy, unlike metrics that count failures.
data.flow: Raw text or tables → needed cleanup/summaries → Jev judgments → fallback for uncertain items → write results to an index or table.
data.analysis: The paper example separates summary costs from classification. The fraud example escalates uncertain emails to a larger model. Preprocessing and fallback both count toward total system cost. Payee candidate generation is unknown; do not assume Jev freely generates merchant names.
data.evaluation: Fix labeled data and splits. Report per-class precision/recall, throughput, per-item latency, retries and total cost. Fraud evaluation also needs realistic prevalence and separate false-positive/negative analysis.

content.title: Content and advertising analysis
content.comparison: Live analyzers provide writing feedback; bookmark-percentile prediction defines a more specific target; historical-post analysis supports retrospective review; ad analysis organizes creative material. Viral classifiers and the X-algorithm simulator have limited generalization evidence. JevMeter applies rules to speech, not validated fact-checking. MaxFusion and StealAds label ads with different batches and dimensions; SEO linking instead selects related pages and existing anchors. Labels, link relevance and business impact require separate evaluation. Ryze spans SEO/GEO audits and fixes; internal linking selects pages and anchor text. Ryze has broader scope but weaker attribution. Neither speed claim provides a complete matched comparison, so their ratios cannot be ranked. X draft-style checking supports revision before posting, distinct from reach prediction or fact-checking; compare subjective marketing-style labels with human judgments. Linked editing checks consistency after changes; Higgsfield connects voice-driven ad creation. Compared with content scorers, measure missed/incorrect edits for the former and complete-production success and generation cost for the latter, not only response speed.
content.flow: Text plus analysis dimensions → parallel Jev labels/scores → explicit aggregation rules → editing feedback, statistics or an analysis interface.
content.analysis: A low score is not the same as a false claim, and past popularity does not establish future reach. Historical analysis supports correlation; retrospective labels can leak outcomes. Claimed use of real X weights does not establish recreation of the live recommendation system.
content.evaluation: Hold out time periods and accounts; prevent outcome leakage. Check scoring stability, calibration, preprocessing costs and a precise target definition. Fact-checking additionally requires evidence retrieval and source verification.

filter.title: Webpage and feed filtering
filter.comparison: The X filter targets posts in a feed; Unclutter targets ads, banners and upsells across webpages. One classifies content, the other page elements, so their rules cannot necessarily be reused directly. Sponsor Skip targets spoken sponsorship along a video timeline rather than webpage elements; caption availability, transcription and boundary errors are distinct comparison dimensions. X reply cleanup targets comments and adds author-described false-positive correction. Compared with feed filtering, action semantics and feedback storage need clarification; flagging does not establish deletion. Needle selects and highlights source sentences on a page, unlike feed filtering or inbox search. Source traceability is useful; extraction limits and unverified recall constrain coverage. webctl filters multi-page search material; Needle locates sentences within one page. The former can reduce downstream reading and the latter aids source checking. Both need miss-rate evaluation; context reduction is not full-stack cost.
filter.flow: Extract posts/elements → apply user-written semantic rules through Jev → hide, collapse or remove.
filter.analysis: Filtering depends on extraction and rule scope. Fast inference does not guarantee no flicker, false removals or broken interactions; page structures can change.
filter.evaluation: Compare false removals, missed targets, initial display latency and per-page cost on a fixed page set. Check normal dialogs, login, infinite scroll and undo behavior.

memory.title: Context and memory filtering
memory.comparison: Tool-history compaction filters the current conversation; memory retrieval filtering selects from an external memory store. Both reduce input at different stages. Evaluate retained information and task quality before comparing token reductions. Compact Adviser decides when to compact; the existing compactor decides what to compact; memory filtering decides what to retrieve. They act at different stages and can be combined; downstream task quality matters. The adverse Hermes evaluation highlights post-compaction recall, retained length, retrieval recovery and repeated compaction, not just one API call. Results for its port do not automatically transfer to other hosts.
memory.flow: History or memory candidates plus current task → Jev relevance scores → select records → construct downstream context.
memory.analysis: Selecting original text and generating a new summary have different failure modes: selection can omit information needed later, while rewriting can distort it. The reported 94% reduction is one quick test, not a default compression target. Updated compaction-plugin sources show budget-fitted conversation context with tool-output bodies omitted; its recording animation makes no API calls. Evaluate size reduction, downstream task quality, cache rebuilding and total cost separately. The case includes the new usage report and reviewer critique.
memory.evaluation: Test delayed information needs, error recovery, old-decision tracing and cross-turn references in long tasks. Track recall, completion quality, filtering overhead and total tokens while retaining recoverable originals.

games.title: Game decisions and solving
games.comparison: Compare three Mario implementations: basic integration, a controlled structured-state/five-action Jev–Qwen demo, and a PPO implementation-effort anecdote. Pac-Man separates planning and execution; Pokémon reports longer progress; chess separates speed from strength; cube-solving code supplies the method. Other demos explore action spaces rather than establish a general leaderboard. Minecraft also uses layers, with local movement/aiming policies. Its performance belongs to the combined system; use the author’s original-speed supplement when comparing responsiveness. Flappy Bird focuses on action timing with sparse implementation details. Sprite Fusion selects terrain rather than player actions and documents parameters and request timing; evaluate reachability and playability rather than player scores. Voice spells and emotion/topic chat games use player input to drive rules rather than model-controlled play. Assess parameter mapping/response for spells and dialogue consistency/classification for chat; account separately for effects and response generation. Jev teacher data plus LightGBM replaces live decisions with a local model. Fixed-route Minecraft combines planning, Jev selection and pathfinding scripts. Compare preparation cost, runtime model, map priors and repeated success separately from direct Jev control. Mario’s teacher later changed to DeepSeek, so new completion claims are not Jev results. As with Jimothy, separate teacher quality, student model, preparation and runtime.
games.flow: Environment state → adapter and legal action candidates → Jev choice → rule/executor checks → advance the environment.
games.analysis: Games can expose grid state, memory variables or other structured interfaces. The Jev–Qwen Mario post explicitly describes structured conversion and five choices; undocumented details elsewhere remain unknown. Cube algorithms come from code, illustrating how overall capability depends on the whole system.
games.evaluation: Fix environment versions, speed, action granularity and random seeds. Run repeated games and report wins, scores, total cost and stalls. State whether simulation pauses during model waits; separate decision latency from real game progress.

simulation.title: NPCs, driving and population simulations
simulation.comparison: Needs-driven NPCs explore behavior; the 500-agent demo explores throughput. Unpaused driving exposes latency constraints. The drone project provides code. Towns and fictional personas are storytelling or ideation tools, not evidence of real-world behavior. Traffic signals, dual-arm manipulation and vital signs respectively concern signal direction, layered actions and state labels. Robotics explicitly leaves IK/physics to code; the traffic ratio and practical monitoring claims lack matching validation. Evaluate each task separately from real deployment. The apple-control comparison publishes single-trial trajectories and physical success criteria, improving inspectability but not estimating success rate. Its replay excludes API waiting, so compare wall time rather than clip duration. The San Francisco demo combines entity types without disclosed action or scheduling boundaries. Separate rendering, physics and model decisions before comparing it with simulations exposing candidates; visual scale is not reliability.
simulation.flow: Simulation state and character goals → Jev decisions → simulated actions → updated state; an LLM may supply narrative reaction candidates.
simulation.analysis: FSD is the driving demo author’s label, not a reproduction of Tesla’s product or real-road capability. Overall API throughput differs from per-character update frequency. Fictional adoption intent is not user research. The drone repository specifies MuJoCo and separates fast control from slower model decisions, while disclosing the limits of its single-run comparison.
simulation.evaluation: Document environments, update rates, pause policy, network jitter and failure criteria. Track collisions, task success and character consistency over time. Compare synthetic-user findings with real research.

interaction.title: Real-time interaction and composition experiments
interaction.comparison: TypeGPU combines local perception with remote semantic decisions. Ask Jev exposes simple judgments. Word/character chat demonstrates selection loops; pixel drawing and RISC-jeV combine small judgments into outputs. These are conceptual examples, not established replacements for specialized models or programs. Other entries cover file selection, emoji suggestions, live shopping and voice-and-pointing canvas control. Their distinct tasks warrant separate cases. Both the canvas and TypeGPU combine perception with decisions, but one manipulates objects while the other changes audiovisual effects. Probably organizes judgments, branches and text generation into a small language. Its hosted site uses recorded playback, which must be distinguished from live local model calls when discussing responsiveness. Shell-history suggestions and the launcher both select a next step from candidates. The former documents thresholds in a pinned version but uses fabricated demo history; the latter selects files. Compare hit rates, acceptance and execution risks separately. json-render assembles interactive component trees, the color experiment visualizes 16-color judgments, and CNVS gates whether to respond to speech. They require structural/semantic checks, subjective matching and false-activation tests respectively, not just latency comparisons. Meeting diagrams combine Jev filtering, LLM structuring and diagram code; try-on combines clothing selection with video processing; clipboard selection reuses text; the Canada map visualizes associations. Compare omissions, outfit selection, paste hit rate and subjective associations separately, including surrounding processing costs. Toothless and CNVS need false-activation/miss comparisons. ReadAloud checks transcribed text, not acoustic pronunciation. AnimeAct adds character feedback with Jev interface details pending. Token, word and character loops need full-response quality and call-count comparisons, not just step latency. The presentation coach tracks outline coverage; meeting flowcharts organize discussion structure. The former remains a local prototype requiring missed/false-reminder evaluation, not an established released meeting assistant.
interaction.flow: Prepare finite candidates or atomic questions → Jev judges → code composes results → update interaction state or output.
interaction.analysis: Code assembles word and character choices into text; the API still returns judgments. RISC-jeV stacks logic-gate decisions and instruction interpretation to illustrate composition, not efficiency.
interaction.evaluation: Record vocabulary size, resolution or character count, loop count and full cost. Compare quality with deterministic code or specialized generators. Measure local perception, remote decisions and rendering separately.

finance.title: Trading and historical backtests
finance.comparison: Monad/Kuru demonstrates on-chain execution; the Nifty author claims live-account use and reports a stop loss. AI Hedge Fund and the Danish-equities experiment concern historical backtests. Execution demos require order, fill and risk-control verification; backtests require time-valid data and look-ahead controls. Speed and token bills do not establish profitability. The five-minute BTC experiment explicitly uses a paper account, distinct from live-return screenshots. Explicit order-book inputs and rules still require out-of-sample prediction, slippage, fees and execution checks.
finance.flow: Market or historical information → strategy inputs and Jev judgments → simulator or executor → outcomes and risk records.
finance.analysis: Historical backtests and live fills are different evidence. Data timestamps, asset selection, generative models, costs and stopping rules affect results. This catalog did not connect accounts, execute trades or validate returns.
finance.evaluation: For offline or simulated reproduction, record time splits, fees, slippage, failed fills, position limits and maximum drawdown. Decisions per second alone have no investment significance.
